scopedClaim.statement: The 28 supplied sorted eigenvalue triples form eight numerical equivalence classes at absolute componentwise tolerance 1e-10. Same-spectrum candidates cannot be distinguished by any function of these eigenvalues alone; this does not establish equality of site-resolved scattering responses.
scopedClaim.scope: Three-site coherent scattering toy and supplied curated pool only; no experimental, fabrication, global novelty, chemistry, Kagome, mechanical stress or hysteresis claim.

preserved: Sorted energy levels, multiplicities within numerical tolerance, spectral gaps, spectral extrema, trace, determinant, and spectral moments.
The X00/X01/X24/X25 class has a repeated level near +1; X12/X13 has a repeated level near -1. X04/X05/X20/X21 has a level numerically consistent with zero.
Trace is numerically 0 for X00/X01/X04/X05/X08/X09/X12/X13/X16/X17/X20/X21/X24/X25 and -0.15 for the other candidates; sum of squared eigenvalues is respectively 6 and 6.1625.
For a matrix with the supplied eigenvalues, its characteristic polynomial and the trace of its resolvent at a nonsingular argument are determined.
informationLost: Eigenvectors, their amplitudes and relative phases in a labeled site basis, and the assignment of eigenstates to specific contacts.
Individual onsite entries, hopping magnitudes and phases, spatial organization, and a unique underlying matrix cannot be recovered from these triples alone.
Site-resolved Green functions, transmission and reflection with specified contacts, directional response, and coupling to external probes require additional observables and contact definitions.
These values alone cannot decide candidate identity up to a physically allowed relabeling or gauge transformation, physical realizability of complex hopping, or experimental novelty.
uncertainty: Equalities are numerical at a declared tolerance, not proofs of algebraic equality. Residual differences on the order of floating-point roundoff are not evidence of a physical splitting.
The packet supplies no units, eigenvectors, full matrices, or contact model. Negative eigenvalues do not by themselves establish dynamical instability.
No response difference between any same-spectrum pair is asserted. The next test requires full labeled matrices from an authorized subsequent stage.
Procedural first-pass isolation is not statistically independent replication: this worker shares the simulator, curated pool and inherited model family.

proposedTest.question: Is the spectrum sufficient to predict the labeled site-1 resolvent for the same-spectrum pair X04 and X20? Given their full labeled three-site matrices H, evaluate G11=[((0.5+0.05i)I-H)^(-1)]11 for each.
proposedTest.control: Before comparison, verify sorted eigenvalues agree componentwise within 1e-10; use the same energy units, site-1 label, numerical precision, and resolvent convention. Repeat each calculation identically as a numerical reproducibility control; preserve the physical site/contact mapping rather than choosing a new basis independently for each candidate.
proposedTest.failureCriterion: Reject spectral sufficiency for this local observable if abs(G11(X04)-G11(X20)) exceeds 1e-8 and both repeat-control discrepancies are below 1e-10. If they agree, this single probe has not falsified sufficiency and does not prove equality of all contact-resolved responses. The test is proposed, not executed.
